---

## Overview

Millimed Co., Ltd. (บริษัท มิลลิเมด จำกัด) is a major Thai pharmaceutical manufacturer headquartered in Bangkok with GMP-certified production facilities in **Samut Prakan** and **Chiang Rai** provinces. The Millimed Group operates through **25+ subsidiary companies** spanning pharmaceutical manufacturing, consumer healthcare brands, supplements, real estate, agriculture, and hospitality.

Their consumer brand **i-HERB**, endorsed by Thai celebrity **Mario Maurer**, is one of the most recognized herbal healthcare brands in Thailand. The company holds **multiple Thai FDA quality awards** and manufactures prescription drugs, OTC products, sterile eye drops (BFS technology), and dietary supplements distributed nationwide through hospitals and pharmacies.

The group's crown jewel subsidiary — **Millimed BFS** — reported **1,423 million THB revenue** and **593 million THB net profit** in 2025, with a staggering **41.7% net margin** and **65% year-over-year growth**. The parent company holds **942 million THB in retained earnings** — they can afford to resolve this.

Millimed's management chose to ignore our communications and failed to protect their data. As a result, we are publishing details of the breach.

---

## What We Have — Over 3 Terabytes

We have obtained **complete access** to the Millimed Group's entire IT infrastructure across **both factory locations and the Bangkok headquarters**. This includes production servers, file servers, NAS systems, ERP databases, email archives, and factory department shares. The total data volume exceeds **3 terabytes**.

## Regulatory Impact

Millimed should be aware of the following consequences of this data becoming public:

1. **Thai FDA (อย.) Manufacturing License** — We hold the **actual BMR documents, QA audit records, and 14 types of regulatory audit documentation** including corrections (CAR/PAR). This is not just database records — these are the physical production documents that underpin every drug Millimed manufactures. Release triggers **immediate FDA review and potential suspension of manufacturing licenses**. The FDA Quality Award for 3 consecutive years ends here.

2. **PDPA Violation (พ.ร.บ.คุ้มครองข้อมูลส่วนบุคคล)** — Personal data of **over 1,000 employees** including national ID numbers, salaries, biometric data, and home addresses has been compromised. The PDPA Office can impose fines up to **5 million THB per violation** and criminal penalties including imprisonment.

3. **Revenue Department Exposure** — We hold active login credentials for **ALL 25+ company tax portals** plus the complete intercompany financial structure across the group. The multi-entity accounting data, transfer pricing arrangements, and BOI tax incentive records will be of great interest to Thai tax authorities.

4. **Drug Formulation Theft** — Complete drug formulations including **Master Formula documents**, bioequivalence study data, R&D results, and regulatory submissions for the entire product portfolio. Competitors gain **decades of R&D investment** in seconds. The i-HERB brand formulas, Neoca supplement compositions, BFS sterile manufacturing specifications, and all proprietary pharmaceutical formulations are fully exposed.

5. **Bioequivalence Study Exposure** — Bio Equalise subsidiary's complete BE studies, including the **contract with Chiang Mai University**, LC-MS/MS analytical data, and OECD-compliant study reports. Competitors can use this data to bypass their own bioequivalence testing requirements.

6. **Banking & Credit Exposure** — K-Bank and EXIM Bank credit facility details, loan covenants, and the true financial health of each subsidiary will be publicly available, potentially triggering credit reviews, covenant violations, or credit rating downgrades.

7. **Physical Security Compromise** — The complete **CCTV surveillance network** (22 cameras + access control) with IP addresses and serial numbers, factory network topology, and building plans are exposed. Combined with VPN access credentials, this represents a total physical and digital security failure.
